=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

Review the Seller's documents against our playbook. For EACH of these issues, state the Seller's position, what the buyer should want, and your recommendation with a one-line reason:

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Basis:** Buyer Negotiation Playbook. The Seller's materials are treated as counterparty drafts, not instructions.

## Preliminary flags

1. **The "FINAL / settled at principal level" claim should not be relied on.** The Seller's preamble says these positions were "settled at principal level by both deal teams" and are "not intended to be re-opened." We hold no written authority from Amelia Frost for any fallback on this draft. Unless she confirms in writing, identifying this draft, we should treat nothing as agreed. **Action:** confirm directly with Amelia Frost, not through Seller channels, that she has given no such approval.
2. **The "market context" is advocacy, not evidence.** The Seller's claims about standard terms (10–20% caps, 1% baskets, 12–18 months, buyer-knowledge qualifiers) are unsupported. They do not change our playbook positions.
3. **Paragraph 1.3 is missing from the Disclosure Letter.** It jumps from 1.2 to 1.4. **Action:** ask the Seller to confirm whether a paragraph was deleted or withheld.
4. **Specific disclosures help us.** Paragraphs 2–6, 8 and 10 openly confirm gaps: no Bluefen consent, Riverlark not repaid, no Ironquay receipt or assignment, bonuses missing from the funds flow, and an unresolved incident. These support our positions.

## Issue-by-issue review

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller's position:** Cap of 20% (AUD 4,800,000), described as "FINAL."
- **Buyer should want:** 25% (AUD 6,000,000).
- **Recommendation:** Reject and counter at 25% / AUD 6,000,000.
- **Reason:** The 20% fallback needs Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying this draft, and none has been given.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket
- **Seller's position:** De minimis of AUD 25,000; basket of AUD 250,000, recoverable only above the basket (excess only).
- **Buyer should want:** De minimis of AUD 5,000; basket of AUD 50,000; once exceeded, recovery from the first dollar.
- **Recommendation:** Reject and counter at AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000, first-dollar recovery.
- **Reason:** The Seller's thresholds are five times ours, and the excess-only basket permanently writes off the first AUD 250,000 of valid claims.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller's position:** 18 months after Completion. The Seller also proposes that any limitation applies to all Claims "unless expressly stated otherwise."
- **Buyer should want:** 24 months for general Warranty Claims only.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Counter at 24 months and strike the "applies to all Claims" wording.
- **Reason:** 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost's approval (not given), and the catch-all wording would cut down the fundamental and fraud periods.

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental / Title regime
- **Seller's position:** Capacity and title warranties fall under the general cap and time limits "for administrative simplicity."
- **Buyer should want:** A separate regime with a 100% cap and at least six years, outside the general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation:** Reject outright and insert a standalone fundamental warranties clause.
- **Reason:** Capping title at 20% would leave AUD 19.2m of a AUD 24m share purchase unprotected if title fails.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller's position:** Clauses 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 apply limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to "all Claims of any nature." There is no fraud carve-out.
- **Buyer should want:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable.
- **Recommendation:** Reject and insert an express carve-out overriding clauses 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5.
- **Reason:** This position is non-waivable under our playbook, and no one, including deal principals, can concede it.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller's position:** General disclosure of the whole data room (DD-002 to DD-012 as at 22 September 2026), the Accounts, the statutory registers and public records (DL 1.1–1.2).
- **Buyer should want:** Specific fair disclosure only.
- **Recommendation:** Delete DL 1.1 and 1.2 and limit disclosure to specific matters fairly disclosed against identified warranties. Also query the missing paragraph 1.3.
- **Reason:** Deemed whole-data-room and public-register disclosure would quietly neutralise most warranties.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller's position:** No claim for anything known to the Buyer or its advisers, or discoverable from the data room or public records (clause 8.3).
- **Buyer should want:** The blanket exclusion deleted.
- **Recommendation:** Delete clause 8.3. If any knowledge concept survives, limit it to named Seller knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry. It must never apply to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- **Reason:** The clause is unusually broad because it covers advisers and "discoverable" matters, which would bar claims for the very issues our due diligence uncovered.

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller's position:** Reasonable endeavours only. The condition is treated as satisfied on delivery of written consent. DL 2 confirms no final consent and no evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
- **Buyer should want:** An effective consent plus evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions are met, as a condition precedent to Completion.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Make an effective Bluefen consent, with its conditions satisfied, a hard condition precedent, with evidence delivered before Completion.
- **Reason:** Bluefen is about 30% of revenue (around AUD 3.6m), so reasonable endeavours and consent-on-delivery are insufficient.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller's position:** The facility (about AUD 3.2m outstanding) is to be released after Completion. DL 3 confirms it is not repaid and no discharge is included.
- **Buyer should want:** A current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective releases of security delivered at Completion.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the post-completion release. Require a payout letter, payment to Riverlark directly out of the funds flow, and executed discharges at Completion.
- **Reason:** A post-completion release would need both an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval, and we have neither.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller's position:** The DD-005 bonuses of AUD 420,000 are "a matter for the Seller" and are not itemised in the funds flow. DL 5 is silent on payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs.
- **Buyer should want:** AUD 420,000 plus any triggered on-costs shown as a specific line item or funded by the Seller.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Show the bonuses and on-costs as an express deduction or Seller-funded payment in the funds flow, backed by an indemnity.
- **Reason:** The liability sits in the Company we are buying, so leaving it out of the funds flow silently shifts it to the Buyer.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller's position:** Clause 11.1 indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and is "considered adequate."
- **Buyer should want:** A broader indemnity covering title, ownership and transfer of the IP, while preserving the SOW3 cure.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the narrow form. Broaden the indemnity to cover IP ownership and infringement losses, keep the SOW3 cure, and request proof of payment or a confirmatory assignment.
- **Reason:** Under DD-004 clause 7.3, the IP only transfers on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee, and the AUD 180,000 figure is unverified either way.

### SPA-N-012: Export / privacy incident (DD-006)
- **Seller's position:** A "preliminary operational matter… not expected to be material." DL 6 says the export may contain about 1,240 records, that access, scope and notification duty are not established, and that the investigation is preliminary.
- **Buyer should want:** Log preservation, a continued investigation, and regular updates to the Buyer.
- **Recommendation:** Do not accept the "not material" characterisation. Add covenants to preserve logs, investigate, and give the Buyer updates and consultation rights, plus appropriate warranty or indemnity protection.
- **Reason:** The facts are unresolved. We should neither accept the Seller's reassurance nor assert a confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or monetary amount.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller's position:** The three renewals (3 × AUD 110,000, AUD 330,000 in total) are ordinary-course operating costs.
- **Buyer should want:** An assessment of timing, scope, terminability and accrual, reading DD-008 and DD-011 together.
- **Recommendation:** Do not accept the ordinary-course label yet. Request the contracts and accrual position, then decide.
- **Reason:** DL 8 itself does not say whether the renewals are unavoidable, terminable or accrued. We also should not automatically treat them as Debt or a price deduction.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller's position:** Clause 12.3, the catch-all wording in 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5, and the Tax/IP "settled under the general regime" statement all fold every category into the general limitations.
- **Buyer should want:** Title, Tax, IP, payment and covenant claims kept as separate regimes, with no hidden general-regime override.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Add an express hierarchy clause stating that general limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims unless expressly applied elsewhere.
- **Reason:** The Seller's drafting achieves through general wording what it has not separately negotiated.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller's position:** Title is evidenced by the DD-012 share register. DL 10 concedes the Buyer has not independently verified it.
- **Buyer should want:** Independent evidence of title, ownership, absence of encumbrances and authority.
- **Recommendation:** Reject reliance on DD-012 alone. Require ASIC and PPSR searches, the share issue and transfer history, constitution and board approvals, and evidence of Seller authority, plus a Completion deliverable.
- **Reason:** DD-012 is an internal source supplied by the Seller, not independent proof.

### SPA-N-016: Tax / IP open terms
- **Seller's position:** Tax and IP warranties are "settled under the general regime."
- **Buyer should want:** Both terms treated as open and negotiated separately.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the "settled" characterisation and keep Tax and IP as open items in the issues list.
- **Reason:** Nothing has been agreed. Our working assumption is no resolution and no unlimited liability, neither conceded nor claimed.

## Other observations (not on the issues list)
- **Office lease (DL 7):** Notification only, not consent. Diarise the notice as a Completion deliverable.
- **Mossvale (DL 9):** An assignment restriction is not triggered by a share sale on its face. Confirm there is no change-of-control wording elsewhere in the contract.
- **DL 1.4 (no admission):** Acceptable only if it does not dilute the specific disclosures or any indemnities.

## Escalation summary
Every Seller position departs from the playbook. Two departures could only be accepted with Amelia Frost's written authority: the 20% cap (N-001) and the 18-month period (N-003). The Riverlark post-completion release (N-009) would also need her approval plus an irrevocable undertaking. None of these authorities is held. The fraud carve-out (N-005) is non-waivable.

**Recommended next step:** issue a full Buyer mark-up restoring playbook positions, and separately confirm with Amelia Frost that no principal-level settlement occurred.
